beats.narration: Begin by framing Course Foundations and Framework Overview as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes work around Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage. Consider this worked case: Govern establishes policies for AI risk, Map documents context and intended use, Measure analyzes risks, and Manage prioritizes responses. On screen, display a four-quadrant diagram labeled Govern, Map, Measure, Manage with brief icons representing policy, context, metrics, and response. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a four-quadrant diagram labeled Govern, Map, Measure, Manage with brief icons representing policy, context, metrics, and response.

beats.narration: Now define Govern Phase and Accountability precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Govern establishes policies, responsibilities, and accountability for AI risk. Consider this worked case: Institutional AI governance policies define who is accountable for security tool deployment and risk mitigation. On screen, show a flowchart starting with 'Govern' branching to 'Policy', 'Responsibility', and 'Accountability' nodes. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Govern Phase and Accountability
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a flowchart starting with 'Govern' branching to 'Policy', 'Responsibility', and 'Accountability' nodes.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Map Phase and Context Documentation operates in a concrete sequence. Map documents context, intended use, affected people, and potential impacts. Consider this worked case: Mapping a biometric authentication system requires documenting user demographics, intended access levels, and privacy impacts. On screen, illustrate a context-mapping template with fields for 'Context', 'Intended Use', 'Affected People', and 'Potential Impacts'. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Map Phase and Context Documentation
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a context-mapping template with fields for 'Context', 'Intended Use', 'Affected People', and 'Potential Impacts'.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in Measure Phase and Risk Analysis and make the decision criteria explicit. Measure uses qualitative and quantitative methods to analyze identified risks. Consider this worked case: Quantitative metrics like false positive rates and qualitative reviews of model bias are used to measure AI security tool risks. On screen, display a split graphic showing 'Qualitative Methods' (checklists, reviews) and 'Quantitative Methods' (graphs, metrics). Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Measure Phase and Risk Analysis
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a split graphic showing 'Qualitative Methods' (checklists, reviews) and 'Quantitative Methods' (graphs, metrics).

beats.narration: Apply Manage Phase and Post-Deployment Monitoring to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. Manage prioritizes risks and allocates resources for response and monitoring. Consider this worked case: Post-deployment monitoring of an AI firewall detects distribution shift and triggers resource reallocation for updated threat models. On screen, render a circular lifecycle diagram with 'Manage' feeding back into 'Map' and 'Measure' to show continuous monitoring. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.
beats.title: Manage Phase and Post-Deployment Monitoring
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Render a circular lifecycle diagram with 'Manage' feeding back into 'Map' and 'Measure' to show continuous monitoring.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Supervised vs Unsupervised Workflows, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. Supervised methods learn a mapping from examples paired with target labels. Consider this worked case: Supervised learning trains an intrusion detection system on labeled attack logs, whereas unsupervised learning clusters network traffic to find anomalies. On screen, contrast two flow diagrams: one showing labeled data feeding a model, the other showing unlabeled data feeding a clustering algorithm. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
beats.title: Supervised vs Unsupervised Workflows
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Contrast two flow diagrams: one showing labeled data feeding a model, the other showing unlabeled data feeding a clustering algorithm.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Data Preprocessing and Leakage Prevention with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Preprocessing must be fitted only on permitted training data to avoid leakage. Consider this worked case: Scaling features using only training set statistics prevents test data information from contaminating the model's evaluation. On screen, show a pipeline graphic with a 'Fit on Training Data' step and a 'Transform Training and Test' step, highlighting the boundary. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.
beats.title: Data Preprocessing and Leakage Prevention
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a pipeline graphic with a 'Fit on Training Data' step and a 'Transform Training and Test' step, highlighting the boundary.

beats.narration: Use Pipelines and Consistent Transformations to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Pipelines combine preprocessing and estimators so the same transformations are applied consistently. Consider this worked case: A scikit-learn pipeline ensures that the same normalization and feature selection steps are applied to both training and test data for fair evaluation. On screen, illustrate a single pipeline block containing preprocessing steps followed by an estimator, with arrows showing consistent data flow. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.
beats.title: Pipelines and Consistent Transformations
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a single pipeline block containing preprocessing steps followed by an estimator, with arrows showing consistent data flow.

beats.narration: Connect Cross-Validation and Evaluation Metrics to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Evaluation metrics must match the task and the cost of different errors. Consider this worked case: K-fold cross-validation ensures robust performance estimates, while precision and recall are chosen based on the cost of false positives versus false negatives in intrusion detection. On screen, display a k-fold cross-validation diagram with data splits and a table comparing metric selection to error cost scenarios. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.
beats.title: Cross-Validation and Evaluation Metrics
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a k-fold cross-validation diagram with data splits and a table comparing metric selection to error cost scenarios.

beats.narration: Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. It also considers robustness, privacy, security, transparency, and fairness. Consider this worked case: A deployment checklist verifies that the AI model's robustness against distribution shift, privacy safeguards, security controls, transparency reports, and fairness audits are all documented. On screen, present a checklist graphic with five checkboxes labeled 'Robustness', 'Privacy', 'Security', 'Transparency', and 'Fairness' alongside brief validation criteria. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Present a checklist graphic with five checkboxes labeled 'Robustness', 'Privacy', 'Security', 'Transparency', and 'Fairness' alongside brief validation criteria.

sources.excerpt: The course will introduce students to the application of intelligent methodologies in computer security and information assurance systems design. It will review different application areas such as intrusion detection and monitoring systems, access control and biological authentication, firewall structure and design. The students will be required to implement a course project on design of a particular security tool with an application of an artificial intelligence methodology and to undertake its performance analysis. Students cannot take and receive credit for this course if they have credit for CSCI-735. Prerequisites: CSCI-331 or CSCI-351 or equivalent course. Contact Hours: Lecture 3 Typically Offered: Spring

sources.author: scikit-learn developers
sources.excerpt: Machine-learning workflows separate data preparation, training, validation, testing, model selection, and evaluation. Supervised methods learn a mapping from examples paired with target labels. Unsupervised methods identify structure without target labels. Preprocessing must be fitted only on permitted training data to avoid leakage. Pipelines combine preprocessing and estimators so the same transformations are applied consistently. Cross-validation repeats training and validation across defined data splits. Evaluation metrics must match the task and the cost of different errors. Hyperparameter selection must remain separate from final test evaluation. Leakage, distribution shift, overfitting, and unexamined assumptions can invalidate results.

sources.excerpt: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework organizes work around Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage. Govern establishes policies, responsibilities, and accountability for AI risk. Map documents context, intended use, affected people, and potential impacts. Measure uses qualitative and quantitative methods to analyze identified risks. Manage prioritizes risks and allocates resources for response and monitoring. Risk analysis considers data quality and uncertainty. It also considers robustness, privacy, security, transparency, and fairness. Monitoring continues after deployment because context and system behavior can change.
